PhysarumSpreader

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_physarum_spreader.Rd

PhysarumSpreader (Wang et al. 2015) lets a resource flow over the network as in the Physarum model, through a ground node linked both ways to every node, with the conductivity of each arc adapting to its flux, and scores a node by the resource it holds after \(t\) updates: $$S_i = I_i(t) + \frac{I_g(t)}{N}, \qquad I_i(t+1) = \sum_j Q_{ji}(t) I_j(t), \qquad Q_{ij}(t) = \frac{w_{ij} D_{ij}(t)}{\sum_l w_{il} D_{il}(t)}, \qquad D_{ij}(t+1) = \frac{Q_{ij}(t) + D_{ij}(t)}{2},$$ with \(I(0) = 1\) at every node and 0 at the ground node \(g\), \(D(0) = 1\), \(w_{ij}\) the weight of the arc \(i \to j\), \(w_{ig}\) the mean weight of the arcs leaving \(i\) (1 when there is none), \(w_{gi} = 1\) and \(N\) the number of nodes.

Usage

centrality_physarum_spreader(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses physarum_steps (the number of updates, required) and the edge weights (weighted).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure uses the direction and the weights of the arcs; an undirected tie is an arc each way. The source reads a weight as a strength; for a cost, give its reciprocal. Loops are ignored. The conductivities of the ground links stay at 1, as the source's equation (10) adapts only the arcs between nodes. physarum_steps, the number of updates \(t\), has no default, because the source gives no stopping rule: as \(t\) grows every score tends to 1, so a stopping rule by tolerance would return a constant (owner decision 2026-11-26). Without physarum_steps the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. On four test networks, with physarum_steps = 52, the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_beta_measure (mean Kendall correlation 0.987, 0.984 at the least) and leverage (0.96); with centrality_pagerank the correlation is 0.84 to 0.91. On the karate club the ranking after 52 updates has a Kendall correlation of 0.989 with the ranking after 10000, while the range of the scores shrinks from 0.115 to 0.0006. The scores the source prints for its four-node example are those after 52 updates. With physarum_steps = 52 the implementation reproduces the printed scores of nodes 3 and 4 (1.0002 and 0.9801) and gives 1.0097 to node 1 and 1.0100 to node 2, where the source prints them the other way round. The source audit found no update order consistent with the source's printed first flux matrix that gives node 1 the larger score after the fifth update, so the exchange is declared here, not resolved. The printed first flux matrix is reproduced. A physarum_steps that is not a whole number of at least one raises a cograph_bad_parameter error, and negative weights a cograph_negative_weights error. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Wang, H., Zhang, Y., Zhang, Z., Mahadevan, S. and Deng, Y. (2015). PhysarumSpreader: a new bio-inspired methodology for identifying influential spreaders in complex networks. PLoS ONE, 10(12), e0145028. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0145028 .

See also

centrality_pagerank, centrality_leaderrank, centrality.

Examples

centrality_physarum_spreader(regulation_net, physarum_steps = 52)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  0.8210857  0.8167787  1.1894243  1.1035349  1.2118676  0.9707841  0.8167788 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  1.2143542  1.0384194  0.8169723 
centrality_physarum_spreader(regulation_net, physarum_steps = 52, weighted = FALSE)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>  1.0087486  0.9928875  1.0196148  1.0035785  1.0099955  0.9903805  0.9861890 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>  0.9886590  1.0008536  0.9990929
